notes:
Passed on the fake backend only (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). The package is model-authored and unreviewed; no hardware was attached, no hardware run was made and there is no hardware backend. The card's GymnasiumDriver is used as written, so there is no decision deviation. fake.py is a pure Python analytic F0 stand-in for the legacy gym/mujoco_py GraspEnv: the action space is the real 200 x 200 by 6 MultiDiscrete (40000 pixel choices), while the returned rgb and depth arrays are 8 x 8 stand-ins for the upstream 200 x 200 x 3 and 200 x 200 camera arrays (GraspingEnv.py:31-32); the real sizes are named in the fidelity gaps and the observation space advertises them. The fake was not compared with the upstream environment, and the sim backend (gymnasium.make for Grasper-v0, whose registration is in gym at gym_grasper/__init__.py:4-7) was not run: it needs the upstream package, mujoco-py, MuJoCo 2.1, OpenCV and a C compiler, none of which are installed where the gate runs. Warnings, all explained: G6.NO_NATIVE_CALL for cap.world.seed.v1, which only queues the seed for the next reset; four G8.NO_UNIT for integer inputs the bridge derives (ticks, action.values, and seed on reset and seed); two G7.MAYBE_ABSENT for reset and observation_space, which GraspEnv inherits from mujoco_env.MujocoEnv, an external base outside the clone (GraspingEnv.py:25), so G7 finds the names in the clone but cannot attribute them to the class. There are no G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warnings. Only cap.world.reset.v1, cap.world.step.v1 and cap.world.seed.v1 are used; no extension ids are needed, so there are no catalogue_requests. The lock's install.python is '>=3.10' because the lock schema requires a string while the card has null; install.notes records the upstream system dependencies. gate.digest is the digest line of the last gate run; check-report.json is regenerated by every run.
